case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.holding: A father who never asked the juvenile court for different services — complaining only to a social worker — waived his challenge to the adequacy of reunification services, and the State's reasonable efforts were sufficient to support termination.
key_cases.relevance: Holds that a parent who is dissatisfied with voluntary or offered services must demand alternatives from the court, not merely grumble to the caseworker.
key_cases.quote: In general, if a parent fails to request other services at the proper time, the parent waives the issue and may not later challenge it at the termination proceeding.

key_cases.holding: The reasonable-efforts requirement is not a freestanding substantive element of termination; it bears on the State's burden to prove the child cannot safely be returned home, and a parent who does not object to services early in the case cannot rely on their inadequacy at the termination hearing.
key_cases.relevance: Holds that the focus is on the services actually offered and the parent's response, so a parent who accepts a voluntary plan and does not object cannot later attack its adequacy.
key_cases.quote: The State must show reasonable efforts as a part of its ultimate proof the child cannot be safely returned to the care of a parent.

key_cases.holding: The element that a child has been 'removed from the physical custody' of a parent for twelve of the last eighteen months under Iowa Code section 232.116(1)(e) and (f) requires an actual change from physical custody to lack of physical custody; mere absence of custody does not satisfy it, and the termination was reversed.
key_cases.relevance: The father's family participated in voluntary services after a founded assessment and the case closed, showing how a voluntary-service episode fits (or fails to fit) the statutory removal clock.
key_cases.quote: Certainly such absence of physical custody would not provide the necessary predicate for a termination of parental rights under section 232.116(1)(e) and (f).
